kind: archive-only attribution of existing alias-body cache answers, guards and general body execution
decision: Do not add a negative cache at this boundary: most direct refusals already reuse intrinsic errors from alias_body_evaluations. Actual evaluation errors need semantic attribution, not assumed cache absence.
limitations: Counts are calls, not distinct tuples, physical allocations, elapsed work or a saved-wall ceiling.
Conditional delegates may hit their own caches; general body entry alone counts that source evaluation path.
Seeded private native aliases and forced depth controls do not establish natural compiler binding, source recursion or cross-tool diagnostics parity.
Standard Rust NonNullable direct-admission control is not native exact type/display parity.
App input snapshots exclude embedded library bytes and failed/transient resolution queries; checked-scope equality is not complete semantic-work equivalence.
Observer-only app timing varies with uncontrolled host contention; no optimization benefit or native <=0.50 proof.
Public native identity/Flatten failures remain failed gates.
No owned heavy builds/checks overlap; replay clone/persistence and lightweight reader tests can overlap.
Replay and three prior target binaries are restored; production checker implementation remains unchanged.
